slides.title: First words and survival phrases
slides.slide: L1 Basic · First words and survival phrases
slides.notes: Say hello, give your name and ask for help in simple English. Notes: teach Hello, My name is... and Can you help me? with gestures and pictures; learners practise each phrase with three partners and point to objects as they name them.

slides.title: Everyday words and short sentences
slides.slide: L2 Awareness · Everyday words and short sentences
slides.notes: Understand and write short sentences about family, food and daily routine, using present simple. Notes: show I eat rice, she eats bread; learners write five true sentences about their day, read them to a partner, and fix the verb ending together.

slides.title: Questions, past tense and short texts
slides.slide: L3 Foundation · Questions, past tense and short texts
slides.notes: Ask and answer questions and write a short paragraph about last weekend using past simple. Notes: contrast I go and I went; learners interview a partner using What did you do?, then write six sentences from the answers and underline each past verb.

slides.title: Real-life communication and listening
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Real-life communication and listening
slides.notes: Follow a two-minute conversation and take part in a phone call, a shop visit or a clinic visit. Notes: play a short recording with a booking at a clinic; learners note three key facts, then role-play the same call with their own details and ask for repetition politely.

slides.title: Academic and workplace English
slides.slide: L5 Specialist · Academic and workplace English
slides.notes: Write a 250-word report or email and give a short talk with clear structure, linking words and few errors. Notes: teach First, However, As a result; learners rewrite a plain paragraph with three linkers, then present it in two minutes with a peer giving feedback.

slides.title: Language analysis and teaching methods
slides.slide: L6 Advanced · Language analysis and teaching methods
slides.notes: Explain why learners make common errors and design a lesson that targets them using evidence from learner writing. Notes: collect ten samples; learners classify errors such as article, tense or word order, rank them by frequency, and plan a thirty-minute fix for the top two.

slides.title: Research and curriculum design
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Research and curriculum design
slides.notes: Design a classroom-based study or a full course plan for adult learners, with measures and ethics set out. Notes: choose a question such as whether peer feedback improves writing; define the sample, the pre-test and post-test, and one risk, then present the plan for critique.
